territorial_scope.description: Applies to autonomous vehicles operated on public roads in California.

evidence.quote: The autonomous vehicle is being operated on roads in this state solely by employees, contractors, or other persons designated by the manufacturer of the autonomous technology.

summary.short: Amends California Vehicle Code § 38750 to govern autonomous vehicles on public roads: testing conditions and $5,000,000 insurance for manufacturers, Department of Motor Vehicles application approval, required safety certifications and data recording, and from January 1, 2030, deployment permits for certain zero-emission vehicles.
summary.long: SB 500 amends Vehicle Code § 38750 on autonomous vehicles (SAE Level 3-5 vehicles; driver-assistance systems excluded). Testing on public roads is allowed by licensed drivers if vehicles are operated solely by employees, contractors or designated persons, a driver is seated, and the manufacturer holds $5,000,000 in insurance, surety bond or self-insurance. Other operation requires Department of Motor Vehicles approval of a manufacturer application with certifications covering engagement controls, cabin indicator, failure alerts and stopping capability, manual override, federal safety compliance, and a read-only sensor recorder retaining 30 seconds before collisions for three years. The department must adopt regulations, may add requirements, must hold hearings for driverless operation, and must give 30 days' public notice before approving applications. Manufacturers must give purchasers written disclosure of collected information. Federal NHTSA rules prevail in conflict. From January 1, 2030, to the extent federal law allows, certain autonomous vehicles of model year 2031 or later under 8,501 pounds may operate only under a deployment permit if zero-emission. The section sets no penalties.

notes: The document contains only Section 1, which amends Vehicle Code § 38750; it has no other operative sections, effective date or legislative history. Subd. (d)(1) sets a regulation deadline of January 1, 2015; subd. (i)(1) applies from January 1, 2030 'to the extent authorized by federal law', and subd. (i)(2) bars rulemaking before January 1, 2027. Subd. (a)(2)(A) incorporates SAE J3016 'as may be revised'. 'Manufacturer' and 'operator' are defined terms, not named entities, and are not listed in entities.

evidence.quote: Commencing January 1, 2030
"Autonomous technology" means technology that has the capability to drive a vehicle without the active physical control or monitoring by a human operator.
"Autonomous vehicle" means any vehicle equipped with autonomous technology that has been integrated into that vehicle that meets the definition of Level 3, Level 4, or Level 5

definitions.term: Autonomous vehicle exclusion for vehicles with collision avoidance systems

evidence.quote: An autonomous vehicle does not include a vehicle that is equipped with one or more collision avoidance systems
An "operator" of an autonomous vehicle is the person who is seated in the driver's seat
A "manufacturer" of autonomous technology is the person, as defined in Section 470, that originally manufactures a vehicle
if the vehicle is a zero-emission vehicle, as defined in Section 44258 of the Health and Safety Code

obligations.summary: Driver during testing on public roads must sit in the driver's seat, monitor safe operation and be capable of taking immediate manual control; testing operation limited to persons designated by the manufacturer.
obligations.conditional_on: Testing on public roads under subdivision (b)

evidence.quote: The driver shall be seated in the driver's seat, monitoring the safe operation of the autonomous vehicle

obligations.summary: Manufacturer performing testing must obtain insurance, surety bond or proof of self-insurance of five million dollars ($5,000,000) and provide evidence to the department.
obligations.applies_from: Prior to the start of testing in this state

evidence.quote: the manufacturer performing the testing shall obtain an instrument of insurance, surety bond, or proof of self-insurance in the amount of five million dollars ($5,000,000)

obligations.summary: Manufacturer must submit an application to the department, approved under regulations, before an autonomous vehicle is operated on public roads (except as provided in subdivision (b)).
obligations.conditional_on: Operation on public roads other than testing under subdivision (b)

evidence.quote: an autonomous vehicle shall not be operated on public roads until the manufacturer submits an application to the department

obligations.summary: Application must contain certifications that the technology meets requirements in (c)(1)(A) to (G) (engage/disengage mechanism, cabin indicator, operator alert, FMVSS compliance, data capture), that public-road testing was done and complied with standards, and that insurance or bond of five million dollars is maintained.

evidence.quote: The application shall contain, at a minimum, all of the following certifications

obligations.summary: Vehicle must have a separate mechanism that captures and stores autonomous technology sensor data for at least 30 seconds before a collision, in read-only format, retained until extracted.

evidence.quote: The data shall be preserved for three years after the date of the collision.

obligations.summary: Vehicle must have an operator-accessible engage/disengage mechanism, a cabin indicator when engaged, an operator alert on failure that requires takeover or a complete stop, and allow operator control via brake, accelerator or steering wheel with a disengagement alert.

evidence.quote: The autonomous vehicle shall allow the operator to take control in multiple manners

obligations.summary: Department must adopt regulations on requirements for submitting evidence of insurance, surety bond or self-insurance and for submitting and approving applications.
obligations.applies_from: As soon as practicable, but no later than January 1, 2015

obligations.summary: Regulations shall include testing, equipment and performance standards necessary for safe operation; department may establish additional requirements, including on aggregate deployments, registration, new operator licence requirements and revocation, suspension or denial of licences or approvals.

evidence.quote: The regulations shall include any testing, equipment, and performance standards
